headline: vend_to_svid_ms: parent sends POST /delegations (t0) -> child's first Workload API answer holding the new X.509-SVID received (t3)
harness: src/experiments/vend_to_svid.py (with the parentsim modes vend-timed and svid-wait), including --jitter-s

code.state: uncommitted working tree at run time

command: cd src/experiments && CLUSTER_NAME=nhi-lab KUBECTX=kind-bench-v2s TRUST_DOMAIN=lab.local uv run python3 vend_to_svid.py --trials 50 --jitter-s 5 --run-id 20261101T223329Z-vend-to-svid-random-phase

jitter.why: run 1 was phase-locked: each trial started once the previous identity had left the child pod, which happens only at a sync of the child's agent, so every vend landed 0.4-1.4 s after a sync. A uniform random 0-5 s wait before each trial puts the vend at a random point of the ~5 s sync cycle.

cluster.kind_cluster: bench-v2s (throwaway, two nodes); the same cluster and pods as run 1, immediately after it

config_changes_on_this_cluster_only.change: `audit_log_enabled = true` in the server block of the live spire-server ConfigMap (set before run 1, still on)

from_spire_server_audit.reading: a sync under 1 s after the entry was created never delivered it; one 4 s or more after always did; in between it varied. The entry therefore becomes visible to agents some time after the datastore write, by a lag that varied from under 1.2 s to over 3.6 s in this run (over 4.6 s in run 1), consistent with a server-side refresh on a cycle of about 5 s. The SPIRE mechanism was not inspected.

anomalies: in trials 13, 31, 35, 45 and 50 the agent held the obtaining Workload API request open for about 0.5 s and answered it with the SVID (svid_window_ms 504-551 ms); t3 is still the moment the child held the SVID.
